title: Present Simple: Negatives
summary: Say what people do not do and what is not true in the present simple. Choose don’t or doesn’t and keep the next verb in its base form.
learningObjectives: Form present simple negatives using do not or don’t with I, we, you and they.
Form present simple negatives using does not or doesn’t with he, she, it and singular nouns.
Use the base verb after don’t and doesn’t, including do and have.
Put frequency words such as usually in a natural position in negative statements.

explanation.heading: Use don’t or doesn’t to make negatives
explanation.body: To say that a usual action or a general fact is not true, use do not (don’t) or does not (doesn’t) before the main verb. The pattern is subject + don’t/doesn’t + base verb. Choose the helper according to the subject.

explanation.heading: Choose don’t for I, we, you and they
explanation.body: Use don’t (do not) with I, we, you, they and plural nouns. The verb after don’t stays in its base form, even when you mention a habit or a general fact.
explanation.example: Our neighbours don’t own a car.

explanation.heading: Choose doesn’t for he, she and it
explanation.body: Use doesn’t (does not) with he, she, it and singular nouns. Don’t add an -s or -es ending to the main verb after doesn’t: she doesn’t work, not she doesn’t works. The -s idea is already carried by does.
explanation.example: My uncle doesn’t drive to work.

explanation.heading: Keep do and have as base verbs
explanation.body: Do and have work like other main verbs in negative sentences. Say doesn’t do and doesn’t have, not doesn’t does or doesn’t has. An auxiliary do/does is needed even when the main verb itself is do.
explanation.example: Nina doesn’t have a bicycle, and she doesn’t use the bus.

explanation.heading: Use frequency words and separate be negatives
explanation.body: Frequency words can help describe habits in negatives: I don’t often cook, and he doesn’t usually eat early. The verb be is different: use am not, isn’t or aren’t with be rather than don’t or doesn’t.
explanation.example: They don’t usually visit the park in winter.

left.label: I / we / you / they
left.note: Use don’t with a plural subject; drink is the base verb.

right.label: He / she / it
right.note: Use doesn’t with she; drink still has no -s.

left.label: Positive
left.note: A singular subject takes works in a positive sentence.

right.label: Negative
right.example: The printer doesn’t work every day.
right.note: Doesn’t is followed by the base form work.

examples.sentence: I don’t know the answer to that question.
examples.note: I takes don’t plus the base form know.
These shoes is plural, so use don’t fit.
A singular name takes doesn’t, followed by like without -s.

examples.sentence: She doesn’t do her shopping online.
examples.note: Use does not + do when do is the main verb.

examples.sentence: Our teacher doesn’t usually give homework on Fridays.
examples.note: Usually fits between doesn’t and the base verb give.

commonMistakes.why: The plural subject my sisters takes don’t, not doesn’t.
After doesn’t, use the base verb without -s.
A present simple negative with I needs don’t before the main verb.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Maya doesn’t her homework on the bus.
commonMistakes.correct: Maya doesn’t do her homework on the bus.
commonMistakes.why: When do is the main verb, it still appears after doesn’t.

studyTips: Choose the helper first: I/we/you/they → don’t; he/she/it → doesn’t.
After the negative helper, always return the next verb to its base form: doesn’t goes → doesn’t go.
Compare pairs aloud: she has / she doesn’t have; he does / he doesn’t do.

exercises.prompt: Mina ___ meat because she is vegetarian.
exercises.feedback: Mina is singular, so use doesn’t + the base verb eat.
We takes don’t, and the main verb stays use.
My neighbour is singular: doesn’t is followed by work, not works.
Use don’t plus the base verb know with I.

acceptedAnswers: don’t like
do not like
exercises.feedback: Their children is plural, so use don’t or do not plus like.

acceptedAnswers: doesn’t drive
does not drive
exercises.feedback: Aunt is singular; doesn’t must be followed by the base form drive.

exercises.prompt: I ___ much time on weekdays. (not / have)
acceptedAnswers: don’t have
do not have
exercises.feedback: With I, use don’t have, not doesn’t have.

exercises.prompt: Leo ___ his homework on the bus. (not / do)
acceptedAnswers: doesn’t do
does not do
exercises.feedback: Use doesn’t + do; the main verb do cannot be omitted.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: My cousins doesn’t live nearby.
acceptedAnswers: My cousins don’t live nearby.
My cousins do not live nearby.
exercises.feedback: Cousins is plural, so use don’t.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: She doesn’t likes loud music.
acceptedAnswers: She doesn’t like loud music.
She does not like loud music.
exercises.feedback: The base verb after doesn’t is like, without -s.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I no want any sugar.
acceptedAnswers: I don’t want any sugar.
I do not want any sugar.
exercises.feedback: Use don’t before want to make a present simple negative with I.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Omar doesn’t his homework on Sundays.
acceptedAnswers: Omar doesn’t do his homework on Sundays.
Omar does not do his homework on Sundays.
exercises.feedback: Use does not + the main verb do: doesn’t do.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change this statement into one complete negative sentence: My sister works on Sundays.
acceptedAnswers: My sister doesn’t work on Sundays.
My sister does not work on Sundays.
speakingExercises.feedback: With my sister, use doesn’t or does not plus work without -s.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say a complete negative sentence using: they / not / buy / bread / on Mondays.
acceptedAnswers: They don’t buy bread on Mondays.
They do not buy bread on Mondays.
speakingExercises.feedback: With they, use don’t or do not before buy.

speakingExercises.prompt: Place usually after the negative helper. Say a complete sentence using: I / not / usually / eat / breakfast / at school.
acceptedAnswers: I don’t usually eat breakfast at school.
I do not usually eat breakfast at school.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use don’t usually eat with I, keeping eat in its base form.

speakingExercises.prompt: The library is closed every Tuesday. Say this with the verb "open" in a present simple negative. Begin with "The library" and end with "on Tuesdays".
acceptedAnswers: The library doesn't open on Tuesdays.
The library does not open on Tuesdays.
speakingExercises.feedback: The library is singular, so use does not or doesn't followed by the base verb open.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make this sentence negative without changing the other words: "Our neighbours have a car."
acceptedAnswers: Our neighbours don't have a car.
Our neighbours do not have a car.
speakingExercises.feedback: Neighbours is plural, so use don't or do not before the base verb have.

speakingExercises.prompt: Someone asks if Mia takes the bus to work. She walks instead. Reply in one negative sentence. Begin with "Mia" and use "take the bus to work".
acceptedAnswers: Mia doesn't take the bus to work.
Mia does not take the bus to work.
speakingExercises.feedback: Mia takes doesn't or does not; take stays in the base form.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct only the negative helping verb in this sentence and say it aloud: "My parents doesn't like fish."
acceptedAnswers: My parents don't like fish.
My parents do not like fish.
speakingExercises.feedback: My parents is plural, so the negative helping verb is don't or do not.

speakingExercises.prompt: Tell Alex these two facts in one sentence joined with "and": "I / not work / at weekends" and "my brother / not work / on Fridays". Begin with "I".
acceptedAnswers: I don't work at weekends, and my brother doesn't work on Fridays.
I do not work at weekends, and my brother does not work on Fridays.
I don't work at weekends, and my brother does not work on Fridays.
I do not work at weekends, and my brother doesn't work on Fridays.
speakingExercises.feedback: I takes don't or do not; my brother takes doesn't or does not. Use work in its base form in both parts.

listeningExercises.audioText: My brother doesn’t usually eat lunch at his desk.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which statement matches the speaker’s description of their brother?
choices: He always eats lunch at his desk.
He doesn’t usually have lunch at his desk.
listeningExercises.feedback: Doesn’t usually means this is not his normal habit; it does not mean never.

listeningExercises.audioText: They don’t play tennis in the winter.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which sport do they not play in winter?
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker says they don’t play tennis in winter.

listeningExercises.audioText: She doesn’t speak German at work.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the contracted negative helping verb you hear.
acceptedAnswers: doesn’t
listeningExercises.feedback: The negative helper with she is doesn’t; speak stays in its base form.

listeningExercises.audioText: At breakfast, Ava doesn't drink coffee. She has tea instead.
listeningExercises.prompt: What does Ava drink with breakfast?
listeningExercises.feedback: Ava does not drink coffee at breakfast. She chooses tea instead.

listeningExercises.audioText: Our neighbours don't drive to the market on Saturdays. They walk there.
listeningExercises.prompt: How do the neighbours travel to the market on Saturdays?
listeningExercises.feedback: They walk to the market rather than drive, so they travel on foot.

listeningExercises.audioText: Ben doesn't have a bicycle, but his sister has one.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which statement about the bicycles is true?
choices: Only Ben's sister has a bicycle.
listeningExercises.feedback: Ben does not have a bicycle; his sister does have one. The negative applies only to Ben.

listeningExercises.audioText: The children don't need their coats on sunny days.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the negative verb phrase immediately after "The children".
acceptedAnswers: don't need
do not need
listeningExercises.feedback: The plural subject children takes don't need (or do not need), with need in its base form.

listeningExercises.audioText: The shop doesn't have fresh bread after six o'clock.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the negative verb phrase immediately after "The shop".
acceptedAnswers: doesn't have
does not have
listeningExercises.feedback: The singular subject shop takes doesn't have (or does not have), not doesn't has.
